==========================================================================================

ADAMS Wave D:  January 2008 through December 2009 (Data Release Version 8.0, April 2013)

Note to Users: This codebook is designed to match the distribution dataset. 
Codebook metadata are derived from the data collection instrument.
If you have questions concerning codebook layout or content please bring
them to the attention of the HRS staff at hrsquest@isr.umich.edu.

Printing recommendation: Set margins (left/right/top/bottom) to .5 inch; print
in portrait orientation using a mono-space 10-point font.

DBWEIGHT       SUBJECT BODY WEIGHT IN LBS (SELF REPORT)
         Section: DB    Level: Respondent      Type: Numeric    Width: 3   Decimals: 0
         Ref: WEIGHT

         Category: FOLLOW-UP ASSESSMENT DATA
         Measure: PHYSICAL EXAM
         

         The nurse recorded the subject's weight in pounds based on the subject's self
         report.  If the subject was unable to provide this information him or herself,
         there was an option to obtain it from the informant if the nurse believed the
         informant could provide reliable information.

         .................................................................................

             3                     997.  Not assessed/Not asked

DBHEIGHT       SUBJECT HEIGHT IN INCHES (SELF REPORT)
         Section: DB    Level: Respondent      Type: Numeric    Width: 3   Decimals: 0

DBVISN2        VISUAL ACUITY - 20/(NORMAL EYE SEES AT 20 FT)
         Section: DB    Level: Respondent      Type: Numeric    Width: 3   Decimals: 0
         Ref: VISION

         Category: FOLLOW-UP ASSESSMENT DATA
         Measure: PHYSICAL EXAM
         

         The nurse assessed visual acuity using a pocket Snellen card, based on standard
         procedures DBVISN1 (NOT INCLUDED IN WAVE D) is always 20, and DBVISN2 represents
         the lower number of the Respondent's visual acuity relative to the standard of
         DBVISN1.  For instance, if the Respondent has 20/50 vision by Snellen card, they
         are estimated to be able to see at 20 feet what a person with normal vision can
         see at 50 feet.  Coding would be reflected as DBVISN1= 20 and DBVISN2= 50 (i.e.,
         20/50 vision).

         .................................................................................
           206                  16-320.  Feet
            11                     997.  Not assessed/Not asked
                                   999.  RF (Refused)

DBNPA          NPI - DELUSIONS IN LAST MONTH
         Section: DB    Level: Respondent      Type: Numeric    Width: 2   Decimals: 0
         Ref: DELUSION

         Category: FOLLOW-UP ASSESSMENT DATA
         Measure: NPI - NEUROPSYCHIATRIC INVENTORY
         Introduction: Now I'm going to ask you some questions about [NAME's] behavior. 
         I have to ask the questions exactly as they're written.  I also am only
         interested in behaviors you have seen in the past month.  In other words, if
         it's something you saw 6 months ago but not in the last month, it doesn't count.
          The questions can usually be answered 'yes' or 'no' so please try to give me
         brief answers. 
         
         A.  Delusions
         In the last month, has (NAME) had beliefs that you know are not true?  For
         example, insisting that people are trying to harm (HIM/HER) or steal from
         (HIM/HER).  Has (HE/SHE) said that family members are not who they say they are
         or that the house is not (HIS/HER) home?  I'm not asking about mere
         suspiciousness; I am interested if (NAME) is convinced that these things are
         happening to (HIM/HER).

         For a description of the NPI, response categories, and information regarding how
         the measure was completed, please refer to the data description.

DDDRSCP        DSRS - WHETHER COMPLETED
         Section: DD    Level: Respondent      Type: Numeric    Width: 1   Decimals: 0

         Category: DEMENTIA RATINGS/OUTCOMES
         Measure: DEMENTIA SEVERITY RATING SCALE
         
         Whether the DSRS was completed

         The DSRS is an informant-completed multiple-choice questionnaire that assesses
         severity of cognitive and functional impairment in domains that are typically
         affected by Alzheimer's disease (AD).  There are 12 items assessing the
         following domains: memory, orientation, judgment, social interactions/ community
         affairs, home activities/responsibilities, personal care, speech/language,
         recognition of others, feeding, incontinence, mobility/walking, and
         informant-perceived stress.  More information about this scale and how scores
         were assigned can be found in the data description.

         .................................................................................

             6           5.  No

DDBLCP         BLESSED DEMENTIA RATING SCALE COMPLETED
         Section: DD    Level: Respondent      Type: Numeric    Width: 1   Decimals: 0

         Category: DEMENTIA RATINGS/OUTCOMES
         Measure: BLESSED DEMENTIA SCALE

         The Blessed Dementia Rating Scale - CERAD is a standardized research instrument
         that characterizes performance of activities of daily living that are often
         affected by dementia.  The informant was instructed to rate whether the subject
         had no loss, some loss or severe loss of ability in a number of areas of
         cognition and everyday activities.  For three items assessing activities of
         daily living (i.e., eating, dressing, toileting), the informant reported the
         level of assistance the subject needed on a three-point scale. For all items,
         the informant also noted whether the loss of ability or the need for assistance
         in each area was due to Mental (i.e. cognitive) and/or Physical reasons.  The
         score is weighted based on the severity of the loss.  The only items counted in
         the score are losses for which the cause is 'Mental' or 'Both' (Mental and
         Physical).  More information about this scale and how scores were assigned can
         be found in the data description.

         .................................................................................
           211           1.  Yes
             6           5.  No

DDMH1          EVER SEEN DOCTOR FOR MEMORY PROBLEMS
         Section: DD    Level: Respondent      Type: Numeric    Width: 2   Decimals: 0

         Category: MEDICAL HISTORY
         Measure: EVAL FOR MEMORY PROBLEM
         
         The next few questions are about (SUBJECT NAME's) medical history.  First, has
         (SUBJECT NAME) ever seen a doctor for any of the memory problems we have
         discussed?  (If no memory problems endorsed, ask if subject has seen a doctor
         for any concerns with her/his memory or thinking).

DEDCODE        Q1 DRUG NAME CODE
         Section: DE    Level: Drug            Type: Numeric    Width: 5   Decimals: 0
         Ref: DT1CD - DT30CD

         Q1.  DRUG NAME - code

         Respondents were mailed a medications form prior to the visit and asked to have
         this information available when the team arrived.  Information included names
         and dosages of prescription medication, vitamins/supplements, and other
         over-the-counter items taken in the previous two weeks.  At the time of the
         clinical assessment, the nurse examined all medication containers to confirm the
         medication information.
         
         The medication data was coded using Druglook, a computerized database developed
         at the Duke Aging Center by Joseph T. Hanlon, PharmD, MS and colleagues that
         assigns unique numeric codes to drugs.  Additionally, in the original database
         each code had a therapeutic category based on the condition or body system that
         it treated.  Over the past few years, the staff of the Duke Program in
         Epidemiology of Dementia and the Cache County Memory and Aging Study have
         assigned codes for newer medications and nutritional supplements.  Many of these
         newer codes have not had a therapeutic category code assigned to the

         Section: DE    Level: Drug            Type: Character  Width: 50  Decimals: 0

DEAGE          Q4 AT WHAT AGE DID SUBJECT START TAKING DRUG
         Section: DE    Level: Drug            Type: Numeric    Width: 3   Decimals: 0
         Ref: DT1AGE - DT30AGE

         Q4.  AT WHAT AGE DID (NAME) START TAKING (DRUG NAME)?

         For medical conditions that are treated episodically, but recur on a regular or
         frequent basis (e.g., allergies), DEAGE is recorded based on when the respondent
         first started using the medication regularly if he or she takes it "regularly"
         for long periods of time each year.  If the respondent takes a drug for an
         infection that he or she has taken before, but never regularly, DEAGE is coded
         for most recent course of medication (e.g., an antibiotic for an infection).

DESTR          Q5 DRUG STRENGTH
         Section: DE    Level: Drug            Type: Numeric    Width: 9   Decimals: 3
         Ref: DT1STR - DT30STR

         Q5.  STRENGTH - amount

         How much of a medication the respondent takes was calculated by multiplying
         strength, or amount, by how many doses were taken per time period specified. 
         This total amount may actually be taken as more than one dose of smaller
         amounts.  For drugs taken in different amounts on alternating days (e.g.,
         Coumadin), the total amount taken over a given time period was used to calculate
         the average daily or weekly dose.
         
         For example, for a medication taken in two doses of 5 mg. each per day, the
         total daily dose would be 5 mg. x 2 doses per day = 10 mg per day.  In the data
         set it would appear as DESTR=10, DEUNIT=2, and DEFREQ=1.
         
         For a medication taken in different doses on alternating days, e.g., two 25 mg.
         pills taken on one day and one 25 mg. pill taken on the alternate day, the daily
         dose was calculated as follows: (2 pills * 4 days) + (1 pill * 3 days) = 11
         pills per week * 25 mg. per pill = 275 mg. per week / 7 days per week = 39.3 mg.
         per day.  In the data set it would appear as DESTR=39.3, DEUNIT=2, an

         .................................................................................
          1560             0.004-50000.  Reported amount
                                 99997.  Not assessed/Not asked
           154                   99998.  DK

DNCPCP         WHETHER CONSTRUCTIONAL PRAXIS COMPLETED
         Section: DN    Level: Respondent      Type: Numeric    Width: 1   Decimals: 0
         Ref: CP_DON

         Category: NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL EXAM
         Measure: CONSTRUCTIONAL PRAXIS
         Whether the constructional praxis test was completed.

         The constructional praxis test in CERAD is adapted from Rosen's assessment of
         constructional praxis (Rosen, 1981), and tests the ability of the subject to
         copy four geometric forms of varying difficulty (circle, overlapping rectangles,
         diamond and cube).  The total score is DNCPTOT.  A delayed recall task is
         included in which the subject must draw from recall the four figures originally
         copied (DNDCPTOT).  This is followed by a recognition trial (DNRCPTOT) in which
         the subject must select each target figure out of an array that includes three
         non-target figures.

         .................................................................................

             1           2.  Subject could not do test due to cog. impairment

DNCPSTIM       CONSTRUCTIONAL PRAXIS START TIME
         Section: DN    Level: Respondent      Type: Character  Width: 10  Decimals: 0
         Ref: CPSTTIME

         Category: NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL EXAM
         Measure: CONSTRUCTIONAL PRAXIS
         

         The time was recorded at the beginning (DNCPSTIM) and end (DNCPFTIM) of
         Constructional Praxis task, and the beginning of the delayed recall trial
         (DNDCPSTM).  The difference in time between DNCPSTIM and DNCPFTIM allows
         calculation of the delay interval between the end of Word List learning trials
         and the delayed word recall task.  The difference between DNCPFTIM and DNDCPSTM
         provides the actual time of the delay interval between the end of Constructional
         Praxis copying and delayed praxis recall.

         Measure: FULD OBJECT MEMORY EVALUATION
         Whether the Fuld Object Memory Evaluation was completed.

         The Fuld Object Memory Evaluation is based on recall of ten common household
         objects, which the subject first identifies by touch.  As per standard

DNTMACP        TRAIL A - WHETHER COMPLETED
         Section: DN    Level: Respondent      Type: Numeric    Width: 1   Decimals: 0
         Ref: TMA_DON

         Category: NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL EXAM
         Measure: REITAN TRAIL MAKING TEST
         Whether the Trail Making Test A was completed.

         The test is administered in two parts, A and B.  The subject is asked to draw
         lines connecting consecutively numbered circles on a worksheet (Part A) and
         connect consecutively numbered and lettered circles on another worksheet (Part
         B) by alternating between the numbers and letters.  The codes for time to
         complete Part A and Part B are DNTMASEC and DNTMBSEC.  Additional information is
         provided in the data description.  Please see variable DNTMATYP to determine if
         oral administration occurred.

         .................................................................................

DNCOWACP       CNTR ORAL WORD ASSOC - WHETHER COMPLETED
         Section: DN    Level: Respondent      Type: Numeric    Width: 1   Decimals: 0
         Ref: COWA_DON

         Category: NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL EXAM
         Measure: CONTROLLED ORAL WORD ASSOCIATION
         Whether the Controlled Oral Word Association test was completed.

         The Controlled Oral Word Association test was developed as part of the
         Multilingual Aphasia Examination and requires retrieval and oral production of
         spoken words beginning with a designated letter (Benton et al., 1983).  The
         letters used in the ADAMS neuropsychological assessment were CFL.  The letters
         used in Spanish-language administration were PSV (Jacobs et al., 1997).  The
         code for the total raw score is DNCOWATO.

DNSDMCP        WHETHER SYMBOL DIGIT MODALITY COMPLETED
         Section: DN    Level: Respondent      Type: Numeric    Width: 1   Decimals: 0
         Ref: SDMT_DON

         Category: NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL EXAM
         Measure: SYMBOL DIGIT MODALITY
         Whether the Symbol Digit Modality test was completed.

         The test requires the subject to substitute a number for randomized
         presentations of geometric figures.  A printed key is provided which pairs the
         Arabic numbers 1-9 with a specific symbol so that each number has its own unique
         symbol.  There are two methods of administration available, a written format and
         an oral format.  The preferred method of testing is the written form; however,
         for subjects who were untestable in this format (e.g., major motor impairment
         such as hemiparesis, Parkinsonism, etc.), the oral version was available for
         alternative administration.  Please see the variable DNSDMTYP to determine if
         oral administration occurred.  Users are advised against treating scores from
         written and oral administrations as equivalent.  The code for total correct is
         DNSDMTOT, and the code for errors committed is DNSDMERR.

         .................................................................................
           174           1.  Test completed
            12           2.  Subject could not do test due to cog. impairment

             3           5.  Subject refused to do test before test began

            27           7.  Other non-completion

DNDSCP         DIGIT SPAN WHETHER COMPLETED
         Section: DN    Level: Respondent      Type: Numeric    Width: 1   Decimals: 0
         Ref: DS_DON

         Category: NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL EXAM
         Measure: DIGIT SPAN
         Whether the Digit Span test was completed.

         Digit Span includes separate tasks of both forward and backward repetition.  On
         both tasks, the examiner read a series of number sequences to the examinee.  For
         each Digits Forward item, the subject was required to repeat the number sequence
         in the same order as presented (code = DNDSSFT).  For Digits Backward, the
         subject was required to repeat the number sequence in the reverse order (code =
         DNDSSBT).  The code for the combined score of the forward and backward tasks is
         DNDSTOT.

DNWRATCP       WRAT READING TEST WHETHER COMPLETED
         Section: DN    Level: Respondent      Type: Numeric    Width: 1   Decimals: 0
         Ref: WRATDON

         Category: NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL EXAM
         Measure: WRAT3 - WIDE RANGE ACHIEVEMENT TEST
         Whether the Wide Range Achievement Test (WRAT) was completed.

         The Reading Recognition subtest of the Wide Range Achievement Test, 3rd edition
         (WRAT-3; Wilkinson, 1993) involves identifying letters and making correct
         pronunciation of a series of words.  There was no Spanish version of the WRAT-3,
         so it was not included in Spanish-language administrations.  The user should
         note that this test was added to the battery of tests after the ADAMS fieldwork
         began.  As a result, this instrument was not administered to all subjects.
